headline: $222,040 airport rental car facility planning funds and new downtown holiday banners.
summary: The committee will review new holiday banners for downtown Bangor. It will also consider using $222,040 in Customer Facility Charge funds to plan a consolidated rental car facility at Bangor International Airport.
items: Customer Facility Charge (CFC) Appropriation – Bangor International Airport
location: Council Chambers, 73 Harlow Street, Bangor, Maine

To: BED 
From: Anne Krieg 
CC: Betsy Lundy, Downtown Bangor Partnership  
Date: October 14, 2026 
Regarding: Holiday Banners 
 
Please accept this memorandum as a request for the City Council to allow new Holiday 
Banners in the downtown district.  Because the banners are displayed in public ways, 
the Partnership wants to seek council approval at the committee level. The 
Partnership’s budget funds the banners.  See attached documents for the decoration 
plan.   
Banners go up during other times of the year, such as the Maine Science Festival and 
Artober.  The Department of Public Works has historically placed the banners as part of 
its operations.

Memorandum 
    
 
To: Business & Economic Development Committee 
 
From: Jose F. Saavedra, Airport Director 
 
CC: Anne Krieg, Director of Community & Economic Development 
Carollynn Lear, City Manager  
        
Re: Customer Facility Charge (CFC) Appropriation    
 
Date: October 13, 2026  
 
 
Consolidated Rental Car Facility – Customer Facility Charge (CFC) Appropriation   
 
Airport staff is requesting committee approval to appropriate CFC funds for planning efforts 
associated with the consolidated rental car facility (CONRAC) in the amount of $222,040. 
 
The Airport implemented a CFC program earlier this year to plan, design, build, and operate a 
consolidated facility for rental car operations. The project is aimed at increasing capacity, 
upgrading facilities, and improving the passenger experience. 
 
The work will be performed by airport consultants, Mead & Hunt, under its 5-year 
comprehensive airport engineering services contract. This initial scop of work entails: 
 
• Project Initiation  
• Data Collection  
• Facility Requirements  
• Site Selection  
• Refined Alternatives  
• Financial Analysis  
• Near-Term Measures for Capacity Enhancement  
• Environmental Strategy  
• Project Management  
 
This project is included in the Airport’s Master Plan and 5-year capital improvement plan. 
 
Airport staff will be available at the Finance Committee meeting to address any questions.
